name: Esomeprazole
summary: The purified S-enantiomer of omeprazole, with slower first-pass clearance giving more consistent exposure across doses.
good: Patients wanting the most consistent PPI exposure from the "classic" PPI family, or where IV dosing is needed.
bad: Cost-sensitive prescribing where omeprazole already controls symptoms adequately — the incremental benefit is often marginal in practice.
clinicalPearls: Marketed heavily as an "improvement" over omeprazole, but head-to-head symptom outcomes are often similar; the pharmacokinetic advantage is real but modest.
mechanism: Identical to omeprazole — irreversible H⁺/K⁺-ATPase inhibition. Only the pharmacokinetics differ, not the target.
pharmacodynamics: Modestly more consistent pH >4 duration than racemic omeprazole at equivalent mg-for-mg dosing, mainly from reduced hepatic first-pass loss.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Similar profile to omeprazole; several days to full steady-state suppression.
pharmacokinetics.duration: ~24h; slightly more predictable day-to-day than omeprazole because less of the dose is cleared before reaching pumps.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: The S-isomer is a poorer CYP2C19 substrate than the R-isomer, so less of it is cleared before acting — this is the entire rationale for the drug.

indications: GERD (including erosive esophagitis healing/maintenance), H. pylori eradication; IV formulation available for inpatient use.
interactionNotes: Same CYP2C19-mediated interaction profile as omeprazole, including the clopidogrel caution.
